steps.u: Convert BerthSchedule from a class component to a function component with hooks. Keep behaviour identical.

steps.a: The mount/update/unmount trio maps onto one `useEffect` keyed on `portId`: load immediately, start the 30s interval, clear it in cleanup. That also restarts the interval when the port changes, which the class version didn't do; harmless but worth noting.

reference.summary: Refactored a React class component for a berth schedule into a function component, replacing the mount, update and unmount lifecycle methods with one useEffect keyed on the port that loads, polls every 30 seconds and cleans up with a cancellation flag. Three behaviour tests pass, but one snapshot test still fails because the old snapshot recorded the class wrapper; it was left failing until the engineer approves updating it.
facts: Lifecycle methods replaced with useState plus one useEffect depending on portId
Interval cleared and a cancelled flag set in the effect cleanup
Noted the interval now restarts when portId changes
